Chinese historian [Xi Zezong](/wiki/Xi_Zezong "Xi Zezong") claimed that the earliest record of a Jovian moon (Ganymede or Callisto) was a note by Chinese astronomer [Gan De](/wiki/Gan_De "Gan De") of an observation around 364 BC regarding a "reddish star".[[12]](#cite_note-13) However, the first certain observations of Jupiter's satellites were those of [Galileo Galilei](/wiki/Galileo_Galilei "Galileo Galilei") in 1609.[[13]](#cite_note-Galileo89-14) By January 1610, he had sighted the four massive [Galilean moons](/wiki/Galilean_moons "Galilean moons") with his 20× [magnification](/wiki/Magnification "Magnification") [telescope](/wiki/Telescope "Telescope"), and he published his results in March 1610.[[14]](#cite_note-15)

Simon Marius had independently discovered the moons one day after Galileo, although he did not publish his book on the subject until 1614. Even so, the names Marius assigned are used today: [Ganymede](/wiki/Ganymede_(moon) "Ganymede (moon)"), [Callisto](/wiki/Callisto_(moon) "Callisto (moon)"), [Io](/wiki/Io_(moon) "Io (moon)"), and [Europa](/wiki/Europa_(moon) "Europa (moon)").[[15]](#cite_note-Pasachoff2015-16) No additional satellites were discovered until [E. E. Barnard](/wiki/Edward_Emerson_Barnard "Edward Emerson Barnard") observed [Amalthea](/wiki/Amalthea_(moon) "Amalthea (moon)") in 1892.[[16]](#cite_note-Barnard1892-17)

On August 14, 2020, the Sacramento Kings announced that general manager [Vlade Divac](/wiki/Vlade_Divac "Vlade Divac") would resign from his position.[[95]](#cite_note-95) [Joe Dumars](/wiki/Joe_Dumars "Joe Dumars"), a former player and executive for the [Detroit Pistons](/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons"), would be named interim Executive Vice President of Basketball Operations; Dumars had joined the Kings as a special advisor in June of the previous year.

Following a month-long search, the Sacramento Kings announced on September 17, 2020, that [Houston Rockets](/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets") executive [Monte McNair](/wiki/Monte_McNair "Monte McNair") would be hired as the franchise's new general manager.[[96]](#cite_note-96) With the Rockets, McNair spent thirteen years working under [Daryl Morey](/wiki/Daryl_Morey "Daryl Morey"), serving in various roles; he was most recently named assistant general manager in 2018. Following this hire, interim executive Joe Dumars was named as the chief strategy officer of the organization.[[97]](#cite_note-97) Other candidates for the position included [Minnesota Timberwolves](/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") executive vice president Sachin Gupta, [Denver Nuggets](/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets") general manager [Calvin Booth](/wiki/Calvin_Booth "Calvin Booth"), and former [Atlanta Hawks](/wiki/Atlanta_Hawks "Atlanta Hawks") general manager Wes Wilcox.
